title: Question 1.3 (Gowers–Long)
statement_text: Is there any pair $(q,r)$ for which one can prove a power savings $G_{q,r}(n)\leqslant n^{q-r+1-\delta}$, for some absolute constant $\delta>0$?
context_text: Gowers and Long [25] proved numerous results on the extremal functions $F_{q,r}(n)$ and $G_{q,r}(n)$, including a power-savings bound for $F_{q,q-1}(n)$, but their results for $G_{q,r}(n)$ were much more limited: the trivial upper bound $G_{q,r}(n)\leqslant n^{q-r+1}$ remained unimproved in general. This question asks whether any power savings over that trivial bound is achievable. The present paper resolves the question affirmatively for the pair $(q,q-1)$ for every $q$ via Corollary 1.4, by combining the lower bound on $g_{q,q-1}(N)$ from Theorem 1.1 with the known equivalence between the tournament and vector formulations.
paper_contribution: Resolves the question affirmatively: for every $q$ and the pair $(q,q-1)$, the paper's main Theorem 1.1 implies $G_{q,q-1}(n)\leqslant n^{q-(q-1)+1-\delta}$ for an absolute constant $\delta>0$, as stated in Corollary 1.4.

title: Problem 5.1
statement_text: For some integers $q\geqslant 4$ and $N$, does there exist a non-transitive $q$-edge-colored $N$-vertex tournament whose longest color-avoiding path has strictly fewer than $f_{q,q-1}(N)$ vertices?
context_text: A $q$-edge-colored tournament has each arc coloured with one of $q$ colours (not necessarily properly); a directed path is color-avoiding if its arcs use at most $q-1$ of the $q$ colours. For integers $q\ge r\ge1$, $f_{q,r}(N)$ is the minimum, over all $q$-edge-colourings of the transitive $N$-vertex tournament, of the number of vertices of the longest directed path using at most $r$ colours, and $g_{q,r}(N)$ is the same minimum over all $N$-vertex tournaments, so $g_{q,r}(N)\le f_{q,r}(N)$; the question asks whether $g_{q,q-1}(N)<f_{q,q-1}(N)$ for some $q\ge4$ and $N$. For $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^q$, $x<_ry$ means $x_i<y_i$ in at least $r$ coordinates; an $r$-increasing sequence $x_1,\dots,x_N$ satisfies $x_a<_rx_b$ for all $a<b$, an $r$-comparable set has $x_a<_rx_b$ or $x_b<_rx_a$ for every pair, and $F_{q,r}(n)$ (resp. $G_{q,r}(n)$) is the maximum size of an $r$-increasing sequence (resp. $r$-comparable set) in $[n]^q$. One has $f_{q,q-1}(N)\le n$ iff $F_{q,q-1}(n)\ge N$, and $G_{q,q-1}(n)\ge N$ implies $g_{q,q-1}(N)\le n$, so comparable sets give tournament constructions. For $q=3$ the answer is yes: Hamaker and Stein's tripod-packing construction gives a 2-comparable set in $[7]^3$ larger than any 2-increasing sequence ($G_{3,2}(7)\ge19>F_{3,2}(7)=17$), and the Gowers–Long construction gives $g_{3,2}(N)\le N^{0.649}$ while $f_{3,2}(N)\le(1+o(1))N^{2/3}$ is the best known and conjectured tight. For $q\ge4$ the authors prove $F_{q,r}(n)=G_{q,r}(n)$ whenever $r>2q/3$, in particular for $r=q-1$, so no such vector construction exists; they also prove that every $q$-edge-coloured $N$-vertex tournament has a color-avoiding path on $c_qN^{1-O(1/\sqrt{\log q})}$ vertices and that near-extremal tournaments must be close to transitive. They nevertheless do not expect the extremal tournaments to be exactly transitive.
